title: Iowa AI Laws

reading.body:
Iowa's only AI law is a health insurance statute, not a technology statute. It bars AI from being the sole basis for denying or downgrading a prior authorization.

The pattern is narrow and sectoral. HF2635 regulates health carriers and utilization review organizations, sets audit and peer review timelines, exempts certain cancer screenings and emergency conditions from prior authorization, and routes enforcement through the insurance commissioner. It takes effect 07/01/2026, having passed 2026-05-13. The AI provision is one clause inside a bill whose main subject is prior authorization and certificate of need.

For AI specifically, this is a decision-rights rule rather than a transparency or safety rule. It does not require disclosure that AI was used, does not mandate audits of the model, and does not govern AI outside insurance. What it establishes is that an automated output cannot stand alone as the reason a patient is refused care, which puts a human reviewer in the loop by operation of law.

The data covers one law and nothing else. It cannot show how Iowa regulators will interpret the provision, whether the insurance commissioner will bring enforcement actions, or whether the state will pass broader AI legislation later. A single enacted law is not a trend, and this one says more about Iowa's insurance market than about its posture toward AI generally.

Iowa has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Iowa

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HF2635: A bill for an act relating to health carriers standards of conduct; utilization review organizations, artificial intelligence, audits, and prior authorizations; certificate of need processes; and including applicability provisions. (Formerly HF 2438.) Effective date: 07/01/2026. passed 2026-05-13

    This Iowa law regulates health carriers and utilization review organizations in prior authorization, audits, artificial intelligence use, and provider standards of conduct. It prohibits using artificial intelligence as the sole basis to deny, delay, or downgrade medical necessity prior authorizations, sets audit and peer review timelines, and exempts certain cancer screenings and emergency conditions from prior authorization. It also updates certificate of need thresholds and exemptions and provides enforcement through the insurance commissioner.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Iowa. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
